decision: Claude Code's SessionStart hook carries no permission_mode, while every other hook does
why: a session's mode cannot be read until its first prompt or tool
evidence: hook payloads captured from a haiku session

decision: the hub records the mode a session starts or restarts in at launch, and later hooks correct it
why: the header shows the mode from the start, and a mode changed in the terminal with Shift+Tab still shows
evidence: hub unit tests

decision: switching the mode restarts the session with --permission-mode, like model and effort, instead of typing Shift+Tab
why: Shift+Tab cycles through a list that depends on the user's settings, so typing it blind can land on the wrong mode
evidence: live check finds permissionMode plan in the transcript after the switch

decision: a session that is offline restarts on the model and effort it last ran on, kept apart from the live status line
why: going offline clears the live status line, which dropped the model and effort a resume should keep
evidence: hub unit test

decision: the status line JSON carries context_window.used_percentage, null before the first reply, and rate_limits five_hour and seven_day with used_percentage and resets_at in seconds
why: both meters can come from the status line the hub already reads
evidence: status line captured from a haiku session

decision: context use is per session, in its summary; the plan windows are the account's, kept by the hub from whichever session reported last and served in hubStatus; the status bar drops a window whose reset has passed
why: every session reports the same plan windows, and a stale window would show old numbers
evidence: unit tests, live checks in the hub and the app

decision: past 80% context the header warns that Claude Code compacts soon and offers Compact, which sends /compact while the session takes input
why: auto-compaction comes near the top of the window, and a compact the user starts can come at a moment that suits them
evidence: SessionHeader tests

decision: a notification goes out for a session that comes to need an approval or an answer, has answered, or failed, only while the window is not focused; a session seen for the first time gives none, and the same state with a later stateSince counts as entered again
why: with the window focused the app already shows it, and updates that arrive together reach the app as one change
evidence: notices unit tests and App tests with the plugin's Notification stubbed

decision: the taskbar button flashes only for a session that waits on an approval or an answer
why: a session that answered can wait, one that waits on the user cannot go on
evidence: App test

decision: a click on a notification opens its session and unminimizes and focuses the window
why: the plugin reports a click on Windows only while the toast is on screen, not from the Action Center
evidence: App test; plugin 2.7.0 documentation

decision: tauri-plugin-notification and @tauri-apps/plugin-notification pinned at 2.7.0 (2026-10-14), not 2.8.0 (2026-10-28); the ten crates the lock file gained are all at least 15 days old; the capability lists the five notification commands used instead of notification:default
why: a release a day old has had no time to show problems, and the app needs only these commands
evidence: crates.io dates of every added lock entry

decision: the notification plugin's Rust side and the Windows toasts and clicks
why: the VPS cannot build the Windows app or show a toast
evidence: the windows workflow builds the Rust side

decision: a path pasted into Claude Code as a paste of its own becomes [Image #N], from a folder outside the session's too; Claude Code keeps the image in its transcript as base64; the prompt hook reports [Image #1] [Image #2] ahead of the text, numbered on through the session
why: the hub can hand Claude Code images by pasting saved files, the way a drop into its terminal does
evidence: throwaway haiku sessions named the colours of test images

decision: Claude Code attaches a pasted image asynchronously, 80 ms for a small PNG and 9.8 s for an 11.5 MB one; an Enter before that sends the message without the image, which then waits in the input box for the next message
why: the first live check lost its image this way
evidence: timed in a throwaway session

decision: after pasting image paths the hub watches the input box until it shows the new placeholders, for up to 30 s, and only then types the text; a message whose images never show is not delivered, with the reason
why: a fixed delay is either too short for a large image or slow for a small one
evidence: tmux and hub unit tests, live check

decision: images travel inside the send request, at most 5 of PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, each at most 10 MB; the hub saves them under its state folder in uploads, files 0600 in a 0700 folder, and removes uploads older than a day when new ones arrive
why: one request keeps a message and its images together, and the transcript keeps the image once Claude Code has attached it
evidence: protocol and hub unit tests

decision: a message with images to an offline session starts Claude Code without a prompt and then pastes the message
why: Claude Code attaches an image only from a paste, which a prompt on its command line is not
evidence: hub unit test, live check after a stop

decision: the window leaves dropped files to the page (dragDropEnabled false), and the message box takes drops, pastes, and the paperclip
why: Tauri's own drop handler keeps HTML drops from reaching the page on Windows
evidence: Tauri config schema; composer tests

decision: a SessionEnd that arrives while the session's next Claude Code is launching is dropped
why: Claude Code runs its SessionEnd hook on its way out, which arrived after the restart for an image message and made the hub refuse it
evidence: live image check, hub unit test

decision: a tool item may lack its input
why: a hub that restarts while a tool runs sees only the tool's end, and the app rejected that message as one it does not understand
evidence: a live check caught the line from one of the user's own sessions; protocol test

decision: the chat shows [Image #N] instead of a thumbnail; a fork's or a new session's first message takes no images; only the message box takes drops, not the whole conversation; no setting in orfoni turns notifications off
why: each is a follow-up that the first version does without
